signature: FECIT GEORG NICOLAVS / OLLER F T IN STOCK / HOLM ANNO 1639”[master’s mark: shield with griffin holding a trumpet].
mouthpiece: Possibly original; no signature, but decoration at top of stem matches ferrules on instrument; dimensions of mp: outer rim 46 diam., rim 6.6, mp exit 13, throat 10, 119 stem.
dimensions: Fbo 12.7 / 13.1 (dual bore; outer slide cannot be rotated); le 5584, be 168, throat (@140) 8
remarks: Two tubular slide stays; hinged handle attached to lower slide stay; mid-slide stay with open work, similar to Öller’s 1640 bass trombone. Repair in tenon 85mm from end. Ferrules similar to Öller 1640, but scallops on only one end of ferrule. slide-bow has saddle with floral decoration and ring with twisted wire; 2 tubular bell-stays, becoming flatter on bell-pipe side; proximal (i.e., lower0 bell-stay has hinge, pin, and eye. Some ferrules have V pattern, while others combine this with a floral design, but all seem consistent. Saddle at bell-pipe side of lower bell-stay has Nuremberg-style flower. Bell-pipe has repair patch 39 long, beginning 678 from bell end; 788 from bell end is ferrule where bell detaches (friction joint). Bell-bow has serpentine pattern as in Öller 1640, with tubular branch connecting two S’s. Nuremberg-style rim wire; floral/leaf pattern on garland, d\ifficult to to see due to oxidation, but it appears to match Öller 1640. This is the only contrabass trombone made before 1800 known to survive. Examined by Carter, August 2002.
